transcript.heading: News Report One (American Female)
paras: A new high-speed railway line has opened in Indonesia, connecting the capital city Jakarta with the major city Bandung. The Whoosh train, as it is called, can reach speeds of up to 350 kilometers per hour, cutting travel time between the two cities from three hours to just 40 minutes. The railway is the first high-speed line in Southeast Asia and was built as part of China's Belt and Road Initiative. The project cost $7.3 billion and took seven years to complete. Indonesian officials hope the new rail link will boost economic development in the region and encourage more tourism. The train service began commercial operations this week, with tickets selling out within hours of becoming available.
Questions 1 and 2 are based on the news report you have just heard.

2. How long does it now take to travel between Jakarta and Bandung?

transcript.heading: News Report Two (British Male)
paras: A new study published in the journal Nature Food reveals that eating more plant-based proteins instead of red meat can significantly reduce the risk of heart disease. Researchers from Harvard University tracked the diets of over 100,000 health professionals for more than 30 years. They found that participants who regularly consumed nuts, legumes, and tofu instead of red meat had a 20% lower risk of developing coronary heart disease. The study also found that replacing just one serving of red meat per day with plant protein could lead to measurable health benefits. Doctors say the research adds to growing evidence that diets high in red and processed meats are linked to various health problems, while plant-forward diets offer protection against chronic diseases.
Questions 3 to 5 are based on the news report you have just heard.

4. How many health professionals were tracked in the study?
5. What health benefit was associated with plant-based proteins?

transcript.heading: News Report Three (British Female)
paras: The world's largest offshore wind farm has begun full operations off the coast of the United Kingdom. The Dogger Bank Wind Farm, located in the North Sea, consists of 277 turbines and can generate enough electricity to power 6 million homes annually. The project covers an area larger than the city of London and took four years to construct. Officials say the wind farm will help the UK achieve its goal of reaching net-zero carbon emissions by 2050 and will reduce the country's reliance on imported natural gas. The project created over 2,000 jobs during construction and will support hundreds of long-term positions in maintenance and operations. Renewable energy now accounts for over 40% of the UK's electricity generation.
Questions 6 and 7 are based on the news report you have just heard.
6. Where is the world's largest offshore wind farm located?
7. How many homes can the wind farm power annually?

transcript.heading: Conversation One (British Male + British Female)
paras: Man (Tom): Hi Sophie, are you going to Professor Wilson's review session tomorrow night?
Woman (Sophie): I'm not sure, Tom. I work Tuesday and Thursday evenings at the campus café, and tomorrow is Thursday. What time is it?
Man: It starts at 6 PM and goes until about 7:30 in the lecture hall. He's going to cover all the material that will be on the midterm exam next week.
Woman: Oh no, I really should be there. My shift starts at 5:30, so there's no way I can make it. Can you take good notes for me?
Man: Of course! I'll record the session too if that helps, so you can listen to it later.
Woman: That would be amazing, thank you so much. I can ask my coworker if she can switch shifts with me, but I think she has a class tomorrow evening too.
Man: Don't worry about it. I'll make sure to write down everything important, especially the parts he says will definitely be on the exam.
Woman: You're the best! I have his textbook, but I'm never sure which parts to focus on. Do you want to study together on Saturday? I could buy you coffee as a thank you.
Man: That sounds great. We could meet at the coffee shop downtown around 11 AM. I'll bring my notes from the review session, and we can go over everything together.
Woman: Perfect, I'll see you then. And thanks again!

transcript.heading: Conversation Two (American Male + American Female)
paras: Man: Good afternoon, City Library. How can I help you?
Woman: Hi, I'm calling to ask about library membership. I just moved to the city, and I'd like to borrow books and use your online resources.
Man: Welcome to the city! Getting a library card is free for all residents. You just need to bring proof of your address, like a utility bill or rental agreement, and a photo ID.
Woman: Great. Are there any fees for borrowing books?

Man: Books, audiobooks, and magazines are free to borrow for up to three weeks. Movies and video games can be borrowed for one week for a small fee of $1 each. Late fees are 10 cents per day for books, $1 per day for movies.
Woman: That sounds reasonable. Do you have e-books and online resources as well?

Man: Yes, with your library card you'll have free access to thousands of e-books, audiobook downloads, online courses, language learning programs, and academic research databases. You can access all of these from home with your card number.
Woman: Wonderful! What are your opening hours?
Man: We're open Monday through Thursday from 9 AM to 8 PM, Friday and Saturday from 9 AM to 5 PM, and Sunday from 1 PM to 5 PM.
Woman: Perfect. I'll come in tomorrow morning to sign up. Thank you for your help.
Man: You're very welcome. We look forward to seeing you.

transcript.heading: Passage One (American Female)
paras: Bees play a crucial role in global food production as pollinators. Approximately one-third of the food we eat depends on pollination, and honeybees are responsible for pollinating many important crops, including fruits, vegetables, and nuts. However, bee populations have been declining at alarming rates in recent decades, a phenomenon known as Colony Collapse Disorder. Scientists believe multiple factors contribute to this decline, including pesticide use, habitat loss, climate change, diseases, and parasites. The loss of bees could have serious consequences for global agriculture and food security. In response, many countries have launched initiatives to protect bee populations, such as banning certain harmful pesticides, creating wildflower habitats along roadsides and farm edges, and supporting beekeeping programs in urban areas. Individuals can also help by planting bee-friendly flowers in their gardens, avoiding pesticide use, and supporting local beekeepers by purchasing honey from local sources.

transcript.heading: Passage Two (British Female)
paras: The history of chocolate dates back over 4,000 years to ancient Mesoamerica, where the Maya and Aztec civilizations first cultivated cacao trees. Unlike the sweet chocolate we know today, ancient chocolate was consumed as a bitter, spicy beverage often mixed with chili peppers, honey, or cornmeal. The Aztecs even used cacao beans as currency and considered chocolate a drink of nobility and warriors. Chocolate was introduced to Europe in the 16th century after Spanish explorers brought it back from the Americas. Europeans added sugar and cinnamon to make it more palatable, and it quickly became a fashionable drink among the upper classes. It wasn't until the 19th century that solid chocolate was invented, leading to the mass production of chocolate bars and candies during the Industrial Revolution. Today, Switzerland has the highest per capita chocolate consumption in the world, with the average person eating nearly 9 kilograms of chocolate per year. Chocolate production is a major global industry worth over $100 billion annually.

transcript.heading: Passage Three (American Male)
paras: Mindfulness meditation has become increasingly popular in recent years as a way to reduce stress and improve mental health. The practice involves focusing your attention on the present moment while calmly acknowledging and accepting your thoughts, feelings, and bodily sensations. Research has shown that regular mindfulness practice can lead to numerous benefits, including reduced anxiety and depression, improved focus and concentration, better sleep quality, and even lower blood pressure. Brain imaging studies have found that long-term meditators have increased gray matter density in regions of the brain associated with learning, memory, and emotional regulation. Many companies now offer mindfulness training programs for employees, and some schools have introduced meditation practices to help students manage stress and improve academic performance. While mindfulness has roots in ancient Buddhist meditation traditions, the modern secular practice does not require any religious beliefs and can be practiced by anyone. Even just five to ten minutes of daily meditation can produce noticeable benefits over time.
